# What happens during a build

A build runs the analysis steps you selected, prepares the final results, then
saves or uploads them as configured. Start with a preview when checking your
scripts. Use a disposable copy before trying production settings on important work.

The [stage-by-stage diagram](lifecycle.qmd) shows the detailed order. This guide
summarizes the supported workflow in preview.5. It does not promise that arbitrary
scripts can be undone or that every original projr feature is supported.

## Check the project and tools {#read-only-resolution-and-preflight}

projcli first selects the project folder and reads its configuration, including
active profiles and local overrides. It checks the selected scripts, hooks,
folder paths, storage destinations and required tools. An explicit `scripts: []`
means no analysis scripts; it does not trigger automatic discovery instead.

Each child command keeps the selected project identity, even if a script changes
its working folder. The parent R console or terminal environment is not rewritten.
Project identity and the folder where a script executes are separate choices.

These checks are not necessarily offline: Git checks can contact a remote, and
optional package setup can require separate consent. A check is not a security
sandbox. Reading configuration and looking up paths do not create directories or
edit ignore files.

## Prepare and run the analysis {#local-production-build-and-restoration-boundary}

Before changing managed files, projcli saves recovery copies outside the project's
disposable cache. The recorded set includes VERSION, managed configuration and
ignore files, recorded inputs and final output/document folders. Declared output
folders may be outside the project. Linked managed trees are rejected. If the
recovery copy cannot be made, the controlled changes do not start.

The production build then performs the selected local steps: cleanup, hooks,
analysis, document rendering and copying successful results to final folders.
Optional `build.r` actions can snapshot renv, generate documentation and render
README.Rmd. They are off by default; see [R build tasks](r-frontend.qmd#optional-r-setup-and-maintenance)
and the detailed lifecycle for their ordering. Temporary renderer configuration
is restored, including comments and settings that were originally absent.
VERSION is written after the local stages succeed. There is no pre-build Git commit.

If a local step fails, projcli attempts to restore the recorded files and folders,
including removing recorded paths that did not previously exist. If recovery also
fails, it reports both errors and retains the backup location. This cannot undo
arbitrary writes outside the recorded set, other programs' changes or a power
failure. Always keep an independent backup.

## Save results after local success {#publication-after-local-success}

After the local work succeeds, projcli saves the selected folders to the locations
chosen by `build.dest`. It uses the actual prepared files before any requested
post-build output cleanup. Git integration can then make the configured build
commit and push to the current branch's upstream. It uses installed Git and your
existing authentication; custom push-only routing is not supported.

If an upload, push or later cleanup fails, the analysis may already have succeeded
and some files may already have been uploaded. The command reports failure while
retaining the successful local release and version. It does not claim to undo
completed external changes. Check the error and [build records](cli/history.qmd)
before retrying. A dedicated analysis-free publication retry command remains future work.

Successful builds and failures with distribution activity retain useful Git-eligible
records when Git integration is enabled. Earlier failures retain local diagnostics
excluded from Git. The pre-Git record is prepared for the normal build commit. After Git is
attempted, its final outcome is saved locally for the next normal commit, even
if that attempt failed. No extra bookkeeping commit is made. See the history reference for exact files and limits.

## What a preview changes {#development-previews-and-remaining-renderer-gaps}

```bash
proj build-dev
```

A preview runs the selected analysis and hooks, but skips production version
changes, cleanup, Git commits and uploads. It restores recorded managed files
after success or failure while leaving preview results in the cache. Your own
scripts and hooks can still write elsewhere; preview is not an operating-system
sandbox and does not automatically redirect every output.

By default, plain scripts and hooks use the folder from which you invoked the
command. Individual R Markdown and Quarto documents keep their native working-folder
rules. `--execution-dir project` explicitly requests project-folder execution.
Bookdown project-wide root overrides are rejected because that renderer entry
point cannot apply the same control. Selecting a project does not rewrite literal
Markdown links or guarantee identical results from an IDE's Render/Knit button.

Plain R analysis scripts use separate child sessions by default;
`config.r.session: shared` selects one shared child for those scripts. This is
separate from your live R console and does not combine hooks or document renderers
into that session. The original projr package remains unchanged. See the
[build reference](cli/build.qmd), [R guide](r-frontend.qmd) and
[compatibility record](compatibility.qmd) for the supported subset and remaining gaps.
